protocol_and_eligibility.review_title: Loop diuretics for acute heart failure
protocol_and_eligibility.research_question: What does this review assess: the effects of intravenous continuous infusion versus bolus injection of loop diuretics for the initial treatment of acute heart failure in adults?
protocol_and_eligibility.eligibility_inclusion_criteria: Eligible studies were individual-participant RCTs or cluster-RCTs; quasi-randomised trials were not excluded, but their randomisation processes were assessed in risk-of-bias analysis. Participants were adults aged 18 years or older with acute heart failure, NYHA class III or IV, regardless of aetiology, ejection fraction, or comorbidity. For studies that did not explicitly describe heart-failure subtypes, participants hospitalised or treated ambulatory with new or worsening heart-failure symptoms or signs were regarded as having AHF. Studies with AHF subgroup analyses were eligible for those subgroup data. Eligible interventions compared intravenous continuous infusion of loop diuretics with intermittent intravenous bolus injection as initial AHF treatment, regardless of dosage or administration rate. Continuous infusion after a single intravenous loading dose was eligible. Concomitant fluid restriction or regular oral medications for heart failure, including oral diuretics such as metolazone, were allowed when used in both groups.
protocol_and_eligibility.eligibility_exclusion_criteria: Excluded designs were cross-over RCTs. Excluded populations were studies recruiting only chronic stable heart failure, people with cardiogenic shock, people with end-stage renal disease (eGFR less than 15 mL/minute/1.73 m2) on renal replacement therapy including haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, and participants with flash pulmonary oedema due to renal artery stenosis. Excluded interventions were intravenous loop diuretics combined with intravenous hypertonic saline, inotropes, vasoactive medications, renal replacement therapy, or ultrafiltration, unless a clean subgroup comparison without those co-interventions was available. Studies where diuretic dose or delivery method was protocol- or goal-driven to achieve a target urine output were excluded.
